Fact.Name: Return files Schedule A (Form 3800)
Fact.Description:
True when the Form 3800 transferee collection holds at least one transfer election statement that has actually been ANSWERED.
It is not CollectionSize > 0, under which a seeded but wholly unanswered statement would make this Boolean Complete true with all eleven of the statement's writables blank — a Schedule A (Form 3800) that prints a header and nothing else. IsComplete-first now, in the RENDER-GATES guarded-presence shape: the collection itself must resolve, and ../form3800aStatementAnswered must be true for at least one item. Pinned by tests/nodes/ty2025/form3800a/form3800a-statement-wholly-unanswered (false) against form3800a-transfer-statement (true) and form3800a-empty-statements (false).

Fact.Name: This transfer election statement has been answered
Fact.Description: The presence test /form3800aReturnFilesThisForm reads, stated once. True when the statement's line-3 credit transferred and line-5 credit earned by the transferor both resolve — the two amounts without which Schedule A (Form 3800) prints nothing — and complete-safe FALSE otherwise, so a seeded-but-blank statement resolves false rather than Placeholder. Every other line of the statement is a certification or an identifier; these two are the money, and the form is the transferee's record of it.

Fact.Name: Schedule A header: transferor EIN (an entity transferor)
Fact.Description:
Question: "What is the seller's employer identification number?" (Schedule A (Form 3800) header, the printed transferor TIN box, where the transferor is an entity). The Form 3800 instructions name this number explicitly for Part III column (c): "If you are reporting a transferred credit received from a transferor under section 6418, enter that transferor's EIN under column (c) for that credit." Asked on every statement whose transferor is an entity; ../form3800awritableTransferorTin carries an individual transferor's number instead. Unanswered: printed blank; no amount depends on it. Validation: an EIN. Feeds the printed statement only.
The single printed box takes ONE of the two: the one-field projection that chooses between them, and the Form 3800 Part III column (c) fact that consumes it, both live in form3800.xml and are owed there.

Fact.Name: Schedule A header: transferor TIN (an individual transferor)

Asked on every statement whose transferor is an individual; ../form3800awritableTransferorEin carries an entity transferor's number instead. Unanswered: printed blank; no amount depends on it. Fact.Name: Schedule A header: the transferor identifying number that prints
Fact.Description:
The printed "Transferor's TIN" box is ONE box (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f3800a.pdf, page 1), but a section 6418 transferor may be an entity, which has an EIN, or an individual, which has a TIN, so the intake carries two writables. This is the one-box projection the printed field binds to, in the repo's existing two-identifiers-one-column shape (cdcc:/cdccCareProviders/*/pdfTinEinColumn for Form 2441 line 1 column (c), "Identifying number (SSN or EIN)").
Precedence when BOTH are answered: the EIN prints. The Form 3800 instructions name the transferor's EIN as the number the transferee reports for a transferred credit ("If you are reporting a transferred credit received from a transferor under section 6418, enter that transferor's EIN under column (c) for that credit."), so an answered EIN is the number the transferee's own return is already built around. Neither answered: blank, which is what the box prints today. Nothing about the two writables makes exactly one of them answered - this fact is the rule, and it is total.
Print-only: no amount reads it. This fact is the chooser for the printed field f1_2, which would otherwise have two candidate facts and no rule. What pins it is the type and existence proof - form3800a-statement-payment-row-h-only answers BOTH identifiers and the module still resolves.

Fact.Name: Schedule A line 4i total cash paid
Fact.Description:
Schedule A (Form 3800) line 4i is printed "i Total of column (ii)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f3800a.pdf, page 1), so when any of the eight payment rows 4a through 4h carries an amount this fact IS that total: each answered row's amount, each unanswered row $0. It is not a bare projection of the Form 3800 aggregate input writablePaymentsTotal, which would print a total the form says is the sum of rows the statement never carried.
When NO row amount is answered the aggregate is still the answer, so the existing single-question intake keeps working unchanged - form3800a-transfer-statement pins that fallback ($18,000.00 from writablePaymentsTotal with no row answered) and form3800a-statement-payment-rows pins the computed total ($10,000 + $5,000 + $3,000 with writablePaymentsTotal cleared). Print-only either way: no tax amount reads line 4i.

Fact.Name: Schedule A line 4a payment date
Fact.Description: Question: "On what date did you make this payment to the seller?" (Schedule A (Form 3800) line 4a, column (i) Date (MM/DD/YYYY)). Asked on every statement: line 4a carries the first payment and lines 4b through 4h any further payments for the same transfer (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i3800.pdf, page 8). Unanswered: printed blank; no amount depends on it. Validation: a date. Feeds the printed statement only.

Fact.Name: Schedule A line 4a payment amount

Asked on every statement: line 4a carries the first payment and lines 4b through 4h any further payments for the same transfer. Unanswered: the row prints blank and contributes $0 to line 4i. Validation: dollars, not less than $0. Feeds ../form3800aline4iTotalCashPaid and the printed statement.
